Website

The website mode runs Providentia’s website on your machine, together with the backend that reads the data and makes the plots.

Getting started

The website mode is not available to users yet; without WEBSITE_PATH, --website only says so. To start the website, give the path to your checkout of ines-providentia (a folder called ines-providentia) and run the following command in the command line:

WEBSITE_PATH=<path to ines-providentia> ./bin/providentia --website

It runs that checkout from its folder: its src is put on the path of Providentia (and on PYTHONPATH, for the backend it starts), and the ines-providentia installed in the environment, if any, is not used. Its dependencies must be in the environment, as they are when it was created with requirements.txt.

It starts the backend, which loads Providentia and can take a few minutes, and then opens the dashboard of the website in your browser (http://127.0.0.1:7782/...). The configuration file and section are not used in this mode.

To stop the website and the backend, press Ctrl+C in the command line. If the backend stops on its own, the page tells you to stop the command and start it again. The LOGS button of the page shows what the backend wrote, to see why it stopped.

Requirements

  • The website mode is only available on local machines, not on MN5, Nord4 or the operational machine.

  • Port 7782 must be free on your machine.

  • The website’s packages (dash, Flask…) are in providentia-env_v4.0.0, as they are listed in Providentia’s requirements.txt; the website itself (ines-providentia, on BSC’s GitLab, public, https://gitlab.earth.bsc.es) is the checkout at WEBSITE_PATH, not installed in the environment.
